bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: regulatory delays in Canada (mitigated by multi-customer diversification); Chinese competition in low-end markets; potential supply chain disruption if customer launches delayed >12 months; consumer electronics and semiconductor bets unproven
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: highly confident, strategic, and forward-looking; emphasized IP moat, scalability, and global pharma partnerships; transparent on guidance limitations but clear on directional momentum
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Axiom Max’s design eliminates priming and includes dose counter — a rare innovation in GLP-1 pens; 18 dedicated meetings at global expos indicate strong innovator interest beyond generics; 68% export ratio suggests deep global integration despite being an Indian SME
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Total Debt / Equity fell from 0.3 at Mar-26 to 0.2 at Jun-26 on a consolidated basis.
- RoCE improved from 35.8% (Mar-26) to 39.0% (Jun-26, annualised) and RoE from 26.9% to 28.2% (Jun-26, annualised), under the deck's "Efficient Use of Capital" slide.
- Fixed Asset Turnover moved from 1.7 (Mar-26) to 1.9 (Jun-26, annualised).
- Balance sheet shows long-term borrowings reduced to Rs. 27.3 Crs at Mar-26 from Rs. 40.1 Crs at Mar-25, with short-term borrowings of Rs. 146.7 Crs at Mar-26.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- Long-tenured relationships with marquee global customers including IKEA, Unilever, P&G, Gillette, Corvi, Lidl and Lowe's, several spanning 10-25 years
- Proprietary IP-led drug-delivery device portfolio (pen injectors, auto-injectors, eye applicator) that has been the biggest driver of growth over the past three years
- Installed pen-manufacturing capacity of approximately 35 mn pens per annum as of March 2026
- Licensed processor of Torlon polymer, a capability for ultra-high-performance thermoplastic applications in semiconductors, aerospace & defence, electric vehicles and medical devices
- Ability to substitute plastic for metal rods in precision applications, described by management as unique globally
- End-to-end capability from design through final delivery, backed by dedicated design/R&D subsidiaries in the UK and Dubai
- Gujarat manufacturing base in Western India, the largest plastics-consuming region, positioned for 'China+1' sourcing by Western customers
- Deepened healthcare leadership with the appointment of a two-decade SHL Medical and Flextronics veteran as Chief Operating Officer - Healthcare
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Export concentration — Approximately 68% of FY26 revenue came from exports (mix of 69:31 exports to domestic), so demand, currency and trade-policy shifts in overseas markets pass straight through to revenue. MD&A frames Shaily explicitly as a 'domestically-manufacturing, export-oriented' company.
- US and European end-demand softness — Continued softness in demand across the US and Europe weighed on Consumer volumes and left Consumer segment revenue broadly flat year-on-year, even as new customers and product lines were added.
- Customer concentration in Consumer segment — The Consumer business rests on a small roster of marquee accounts - IKEA, Unilever, P&G, Gillette, Corvi, Lidl and Lowe's - so the loss or volume reduction of any one long-standing relationship is material.
- Dependence on the GLP-1 / semaglutide device opportunity — Healthcare has been the biggest growth driver over the past three years and is tied to the semaglutide patent cliff, which opened in only eight markets in 2026 while the core US, EU and Japan markets remain patent-protected until 2031-32; regulatory pathways differ by market (biosimilar testing in Brazil, India and South Africa versus bioequivalence-only in Canada and Saudi Arabia), and India already saw more than 40 generic brands launch, implying crowded, competitive device demand.
- Technology substitution in drug delivery — Oral GLP-1 formulations and wearable patch injectors compete with pen and auto-injector formats; MD&A notes oral formats at roughly 6-7% of GLP-1 administration and cites that more than 75% of the 55-60 molecules in development remain injectable as the reason near-term substitution risk is limited - a limit that erodes if the injectable share falls.
- Geopolitical and supply-chain disruption, energy and freight costs — MD&A records that geopolitical tensions and evolving trade policies raised volatility, energy prices and freight costs and disrupted global supply chains during early 2026, with the Middle East conflict at end-February 2026 the principal swing factor behind the IMF's global growth downgrade to 3.1% for 2026.
- Raw-material and commodity price volatility — The business converts polymer feedstock whose price tracks crude and petrochemical markets; MD&A flags commodity price fluctuations as a key risk to the Indian growth backdrop and notes Brent crude forecasts among its macro exhibits.
- Geographic concentration of manufacturing in Gujarat — Manufacturing sits at a single Gujarat base (Halol and Rania), concentrating operational, regulatory and event risk in one state, albeit within Western India, the largest plastics-consuming region at 46.55% of national consumption.

business.body:

- Credit rating slide cites a "Long and established track record in the plastic injection molding business along with experienced Promoters" and "New business confirmations from existing clients along with addition of marquee clients across diversified industries".

business.title: Notable from the deck

business.body: Shaily designs and manufactures precision plastic and engineered products across three businesses: a Consumer segment covering home furnishings, personal-care and FMCG packaging and carbon-steel furniture; a Healthcare segment comprising proprietary IP-led pen injectors, auto-injectors, other specialty drug-delivery devices, an eye applicator and primary pharmaceutical packaging; and an Industrial segment of automotive components, appliance casings, LED lighting and high-performance engineering products. It offers end-to-end capability from design through final delivery and serves marquee global customers, with several relationships spanning 10-25 years. Its Gujarat manufacturing base at Halol and Rania supplies largely export markets, supported by design and R&D subsidiaries in the UK and Dubai.

outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Scale the IP-led Healthcare segment - pen injectors, auto-injectors, specialty drug-delivery devices and eye applicator - which management describes as the biggest driver of growth over the past three years, backed by expanded pen capacity and a dedicated Healthcare COO appointed effective 1 March 2026
- Position as an export-oriented Indian manufacturing base for Western customers pursuing 'China+1' sourcing diversification, leveraging quality-driven, globally-certified capability
- Broaden the Consumer segment by adding new customers and product lines to offset soft US and European demand, offering end-to-end capability from design to final delivery across kitchenware, integrated cooking, dining and storage solutions
- Build high-performance engineering-plastics capability as a licensed Torlon processor for semiconductors, aerospace & defence, electric vehicles and medical devices, including plastic-for-metal substitution in precision applications
- Run design and R&D through overseas subsidiaries - Shaily Innovations Limited (UK) as a design centre and R&D division for medical and drug-delivery devices, and Shaily Innovations FZCO (Dubai) for design and development services on drug-delivery device contracts
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Shaily's expansion in FY26 was concentrated in the Healthcare segment. Installed pen-manufacturing capacity was expanded to approximately 35 mn pens per annum as of March 2026, and management appointed Mr. Chi Hung Kam ('Joe' Kam), a two-decade SHL Medical and Flextronics veteran with experience managing nine manufacturing sites across Taiwan and the US, as Chief Operating Officer - Healthcare effective 1 March 2026, explicitly reflecting the scale-up ambitions for the segment. The manufacturing footprint remains the Gujarat base at Halol and Rania. Design and development capacity sits offshore in two wholly owned subsidiaries: Shaily Innovations Limited (formerly Shaily (UK) Limited) in the United Kingdom, which operates as a Design Centre and R&D division for medical and drug-delivery devices, and Shaily Innovations FZCO, incorporated in Dubai, UAE on 1 January 2025, engaged in design and development services for drug-delivery device contracts. The Company has no associate or joint venture company, and the Directors' Report records no material changes or commitments from the close of the year to the date of the report.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Semaglutide patent and data-exclusivity expiry began in a first wave of eight markets in 2026 (Canada, Brazil, China, India, Mexico, Turkey, Saudi Arabia, South Africa), together roughly 33-38% of the world's obese adult population, with India's patent expiring 20 March 2026 and more than 40 generic brands launched - a structural demand event for drug-delivery devices
- More than 75% of the 55-60 GLP-1 molecules currently in development remain injectable, limiting near-term substitution risk from oral formats; auto-injectors hold an estimated 58% device-share of GLP-1 administration
- Global pen and injector drug-delivery device market projected to grow from approximately USD 114.7 billion in 2025 to USD 236.5 billion by 2033, with the GLP-1/insulin-style pen injector sub-market projected to exceed USD 60 billion by 2030
- India's medical devices market projected to grow at approximately 16.4% CAGR to USD 50.1 billion by 2030, roughly 2.5x the global pace, supported by the National Medical Devices Policy 2023
- Continued softness in Consumer demand across the US and Europe weighed on volumes, keeping Consumer segment revenue broadly flat year-on-year
- Industrial demand supported by 'lightweighting' - substitution of metal with engineered plastics in automotive and industrial applications - reinforced by tightening emissions regulation and the shift to electric vehicles
- India's plastics industry growth underpinned by PLI-driven polymer capacity additions in Gujarat, quick-commerce demand for rigid food-grade containers, HDPE piping under Swachh Bharat Mission Phase-II, electric two-wheeler engineering plastics, and rising pharmaceutical exports lifting medical-grade resin consumption in Gujarat and Maharashtra
- Western India, where Shaily's Halol and Rania base sits, accounts for the largest share of national plastics consumption at 46.55%, and 'Make in India' plus 'China+1' preference among Western customers creates sourcing opportunities
- Export orientation - approximately 68% of FY26 revenue from exports - makes the domestically-manufacturing, export-led model sensitive to global demand and trade policy
- Global macro backdrop is a headwind: IMF projects global growth moderating to 3.1% in 2026 with headline inflation at 4.4%, driven by geopolitical tensions, higher energy prices and elevated freight costs
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: Shaily delivered 34% revenue growth and 1,030 bps EBITDA margin expansion driven by explosive 163% growth in Healthcare segment, now 38% of revenue, as its next-gen Axiom Max GLP-1 pen gains traction and capacity expands to 80M pens by FY26 end — this structural shift from commodity plastics to high-margin, IP-led device manufacturing is redefining its valuation multiple and creating a durable moat.

risks.note: Approximately 68% of FY26 revenue came from exports (mix of 69:31 exports to domestic), so demand, currency and trade-policy shifts in overseas markets pass straight through to revenue. MD&A frames Shaily explicitly as a 'domestically-manufacturing, export-oriented' company.
Continued softness in demand across the US and Europe weighed on Consumer volumes and left Consumer segment revenue broadly flat year-on-year, even as new customers and product lines were added.

The Consumer business rests on a small roster of marquee accounts - IKEA, Unilever, P&G, Gillette, Corvi, Lidl and Lowe's - so the loss or volume reduction of any one long-standing relationship is material.

risks.risk: Dependence on the GLP-1 / semaglutide device opportunity
risks.note: Healthcare has been the biggest growth driver over the past three years and is tied to the semaglutide patent cliff, which opened in only eight markets in 2026 while the core US, EU and Japan markets remain patent-protected until 2031-32; regulatory pathways differ by market (biosimilar testing in Brazil, India and South Africa versus bioequivalence-only in Canada and Saudi Arabia), and India already saw more than 40 generic brands launch, implying crowded, competitive device demand.

Oral GLP-1 formulations and wearable patch injectors compete with pen and auto-injector formats; MD&A notes oral formats at roughly 6-7% of GLP-1 administration and cites that more than 75% of the 55-60 molecules in development remain injectable as the reason near-term substitution risk is limited - a limit that erodes if the injectable share falls.

risks.risk: Geopolitical and supply-chain disruption, energy and freight costs
risks.note: MD&A records that geopolitical tensions and evolving trade policies raised volatility, energy prices and freight costs and disrupted global supply chains during early 2026, with the Middle East conflict at end-February 2026 the principal swing factor behind the IMF's global growth downgrade to 3.1% for 2026.

The business converts polymer feedstock whose price tracks crude and petrochemical markets; MD&A flags commodity price fluctuations as a key risk to the Indian growth backdrop and notes Brent crude forecasts among its macro exhibits.

risks.risk: Geographic concentration of manufacturing in Gujarat
risks.note: Manufacturing sits at a single Gujarat base (Halol and Rania), concentrating operational, regulatory and event risk in one state, albeit within Western India, the largest plastics-consuming region at 46.55% of national consumption.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Shaily Engineering Plastics is a Gujarat-based, export-oriented precision injection-moulding and contract manufacturer spanning consumer/home furnishings, IP-led healthcare drug-delivery devices and industrial engineering plastics, deriving approximately 68% of FY26 revenue from exports.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Shaily designs and manufactures precision plastic and engineered products across three businesses: a Consumer segment covering home furnishings, personal-care and FMCG packaging and carbon-steel furniture; a Healthcare segment comprising proprietary IP-led pen injectors, auto-injectors, other specialty drug-delivery devices, an eye applicator and primary pharmaceutical packaging; and an Industrial segment of automotive components, appliance casings, LED lighting and high-performance engineering products. It offers end-to-end capability from design through final delivery and serves marquee global customers, with several relationships spanning 10-25 years. Its Gujarat manufacturing base at Halol and Rania supplies largely export markets, supported by design and R&D subsidiaries in the UK and Dubai.

group_structure.title: Group structure (profile)
group_structure.body:
- Shaily Innovations Limited (formerly Shaily (UK) Limited) — subsidiary: Wholly owned subsidiary (100%) in the United Kingdom, acquired 15th September 2021; operates as a Design Centre and Research & Development division for medical and drug delivery devices. Ceased to be a material subsidiary under SEBI Listing Regulations as per the FY26 audited financial statements.
- Shaily Innovations FZCO — subsidiary: Wholly owned subsidiary (100%) incorporated in Dubai, UAE on 01st January 2025; engaged in design and development services for drug delivery device contracts.
- Panax Appliances Pvt. Ltd. — related party: Entity in which key management personnel have significant influence.
- Shaily-IDC India Pvt. Ltd. — related party: Entity in which key management personnel have significant influence.
- Shaily Medical Plastics Pvt. Ltd. — related party: Entity in which key management personnel have significant influence.
- Jariwala Shah Kanji Raichand & Co — related party: Firm owned by a relative of key management personnel.
- Buddha Bambu (Mrs. Purnima Shah) — related party: Firm owned by a relative of key management personnel.
- Tiivra Ventures Private Limited — related party: Entity in which Independent Directors have significant influence.

products.body:

- **Healthcare:** Pen injectors, Auto-injectors, Specialty drug-delivery devices, Eye applicator, Primary pharmaceutical packaging
- **Industrial:** Automotive components including knobs and switchgear parts, Appliance casings, LED lighting, High-performance engineering products

growth_optionality.body: Consumer Electronics: commercial supply to begin H2 FY26; semiconductor component opportunity under active development; potential for $20M-$100M business in 3-5 years; U.K. innovation unit expanding into patch pumps and on-body injectors

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Semaglutide patent and data-exclusivity expiry began in a first wave of eight markets in 2026 (Canada, Brazil, China, India, Mexico, Turkey, Saudi Arabia, South Africa), together roughly 33-38% of the world's obese adult population, with India's patent expiring 20 March 2026 and more than 40 generic brands launched - a structural demand event for drug-delivery devices
- More than 75% of the 55-60 GLP-1 molecules currently in development remain injectable, limiting near-term substitution risk from oral formats; auto-injectors hold an estimated 58% device-share of GLP-1 administration
- Global pen and injector drug-delivery device market projected to grow from approximately USD 114.7 billion in 2025 to USD 236.5 billion by 2033, with the GLP-1/insulin-style pen injector sub-market projected to exceed USD 60 billion by 2030
- India's medical devices market projected to grow at approximately 16.4% CAGR to USD 50.1 billion by 2030, roughly 2.5x the global pace, supported by the National Medical Devices Policy 2023
- Continued softness in Consumer demand across the US and Europe weighed on volumes, keeping Consumer segment revenue broadly flat year-on-year
- Industrial demand supported by 'lightweighting' - substitution of metal with engineered plastics in automotive and industrial applications - reinforced by tightening emissions regulation and the shift to electric vehicles
- India's plastics industry growth underpinned by PLI-driven polymer capacity additions in Gujarat, quick-commerce demand for rigid food-grade containers, HDPE piping under Swachh Bharat Mission Phase-II, electric two-wheeler engineering plastics, and rising pharmaceutical exports lifting medical-grade resin consumption in Gujarat and Maharashtra
- Western India, where Shaily's Halol and Rania base sits, accounts for the largest share of national plastics consumption at 46.55%, and 'Make in India' plus 'China+1' preference among Western customers creates sourcing opportunities
- Export orientation - approximately 68% of FY26 revenue from exports - makes the domestically-manufacturing, export-led model sensitive to global demand and trade policy
- Global macro backdrop is a headwind: IMF projects global growth moderating to 3.1% in 2026 with headline inflation at 4.4%, driven by geopolitical tensions, higher energy prices and elevated freight costs

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: EBITDA margin expanded due to higher mix of IP-led devices (Axiom Max, Neo) with better gross margins; cost leverage from scale; no material input cost inflation cited; margin sustainability supported by product mix shift

capital_allocation.body: 94,500 stock options granted to employees; debt-to-equity at 0.3x; ROCE 42.3%, ROE 32.7%; capital disciplined, no dividend policy mentioned

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Shaily's expansion in FY26 was concentrated in the Healthcare segment. Installed pen-manufacturing capacity was expanded to approximately 35 mn pens per annum as of March 2026, and management appointed Mr. Chi Hung Kam ('Joe' Kam), a two-decade SHL Medical and Flextronics veteran with experience managing nine manufacturing sites across Taiwan and the US, as Chief Operating Officer - Healthcare effective 1 March 2026, explicitly reflecting the scale-up ambitions for the segment. The manufacturing footprint remains the Gujarat base at Halol and Rania. Design and development capacity sits offshore in two wholly owned subsidiaries: Shaily Innovations Limited (formerly Shaily (UK) Limited) in the United Kingdom, which operates as a Design Centre and R&D division for medical and drug-delivery devices, and Shaily Innovations FZCO, incorporated in Dubai, UAE on 1 January 2025, engaged in design and development services for drug-delivery device contracts. The Company has no associate or joint venture company, and the Directors' Report records no material changes or commitments from the close of the year to the date of the report.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: highly confident, strategic, and forward-looking; emphasized IP moat, scalability, and global pharma partnerships; transparent on guidance limitations but clear on directional momentum

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Long-tenured relationships with marquee global customers including IKEA, Unilever, P&G, Gillette, Corvi, Lidl and Lowe's, several spanning 10-25 years
- Proprietary IP-led drug-delivery device portfolio (pen injectors, auto-injectors, eye applicator) that has been the biggest driver of growth over the past three years
- Installed pen-manufacturing capacity of approximately 35 mn pens per annum as of March 2026
- Licensed processor of Torlon polymer, a capability for ultra-high-performance thermoplastic applications in semiconductors, aerospace & defence, electric vehicles and medical devices
- Ability to substitute plastic for metal rods in precision applications, described by management as unique globally
- End-to-end capability from design through final delivery, backed by dedicated design/R&D subsidiaries in the UK and Dubai
- Gujarat manufacturing base in Western India, the largest plastics-consuming region, positioned for 'China+1' sourcing by Western customers
- Deepened healthcare leadership with the appointment of a two-decade SHL Medical and Flextronics veteran as Chief Operating Officer - Healthcare

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: regulatory delays in Canada (mitigated by multi-customer diversification); Chinese competition in low-end markets; potential supply chain disruption if customer launches delayed >12 months; consumer electronics and semiconductor bets unproven

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: Axiom Max’s design eliminates priming and includes dose counter — a rare innovation in GLP-1 pens; 18 dedicated meetings at global expos indicate strong innovator interest beyond generics; 68% export ratio suggests deep global integration despite being an Indian SME

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Scale the IP-led Healthcare segment - pen injectors, auto-injectors, specialty drug-delivery devices and eye applicator - which management describes as the biggest driver of growth over the past three years, backed by expanded pen capacity and a dedicated Healthcare COO appointed effective 1 March 2026
- Position as an export-oriented Indian manufacturing base for Western customers pursuing 'China+1' sourcing diversification, leveraging quality-driven, globally-certified capability
- Broaden the Consumer segment by adding new customers and product lines to offset soft US and European demand, …

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Credit rating] CARE A+ ; Outlook: Stable (Rating Action: Reaffirmed) on Long Term Bank Facilities of Rs. 239.62 Crs., and CARE A1 (Reaffirmed) on Short Term Bank Facilities of Rs. 35 Crs. — footnoted "Updated as on 30th September 2025".
- [Group scope] The Q1 FY27 consolidated financial highlights carry the footnote "* Includes the UK & UAE Subsidiary Business", so consolidated figures are not the standalone Indian entity alone.
- [Mix shift] Domestic-vs-export revenue mix moved between the pair 76.1% / 23.9% (Q1 FY26) and 58.1% / 41.9% (Q1 FY27); the extracted chart does not bind which share is Export and which is Domestic, so the direction is not asserted here. The deck's own note reads: "The shift in the domestic-export mix is primarily due to the growing Healthcare business, where supplies to Indian pharma customers ultimately cater to global markets."
